headline: A Weak Password Opens Denmark’s CPR Register
lede: Three accounts, including an administrator, reportedly used 123456 while attackers queried Denmark’s civil-registration system for nearly 22 days. The breach exposed data associated with roughly 8.8 million CPR numbers—and the governance around third-party access.

headline: REA Gives Agents a Reverse-Engineering Workbench
lede: REA connects coding agents to live applications, JavaScript packages, native binaries, and browser processes. It observes, tests, and explains software that its builders cannot simply read—turning reverse engineering into a repeatable workflow.

headline: A Telegram Link Could Steal Local Files
lede: Telegram Desktop accepted crafted input through its local IPC socket, letting one clicked link read files and upload them to an attacker-controlled chat. Version 7.2.9 removes the vulnerable mechanism; older clients should not linger.

headline: Cloudflare Buys Deno, Then Winds It Down
lede: Deno’s team is joining Cloudflare, but the independent runtime and Deno Deploy now have clocks running. Runtime updates end after one year; the hosting service shuts down in six months, leaving users to plan their migrations.

headline: Minesweeper Gets the Triple-A Treatment
lede: The humble grid arrives with blockbuster ambitions: drama, tutorials, dialogue, and credits wrapped around a familiar puzzle. It is an affectionate parody of modern game excess, rendered with enough polish to make the joke land.

headline: WSL3 Moves Faster—Within Limits
lede: Across tested workloads, WSL3 ranges from a modest improvement to a substantial gain over WSL2. Memory and IPC-heavy tasks benefit most; a GoReleaser build moves only about four percent faster overall.

headline: The Eye of Sauron Finds Cameras in the Dark
lede: ESauron listens for electromagnetic traces produced as hidden cameras encode and store images. In tests across 50 devices, deliberate scene changes helped locate every camera from more than 20 meters away—even when the devices were offline.

headline: Processing Changes More Than the Nutrition Label
lede: In a controlled study of 57 adults, matched meals produced different insulin, blood-sugar, energy-expenditure, and brain-activity responses depending on processing level. The findings suggest that food structure and formulation matter, while the small, short-term design counsels restraint.

headline: Computers Do Not Carry the Blame
lede: The essay rejects the convenient fiction that an AI system can absorb responsibility for the decisions made around it. Designers, deployers, and companies still choose the permissions, incentives, and guardrails that shape an outcome.
pullquote: Delegating a decision does not delegate responsibility.

headline: Cube Type Turns Words Into Isometric Blocks
lede: Cube Type is a browser playground for arranging text as geometric, cube-like letterforms. With line wrapping, manual breaks, and simple positioning controls, it keeps the experiment focused: type in, compose, and inspect the shape.
